title: Effects of Different Instrument Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization Force Applications on Ankle Stiffness and Dorsiflexion
official: Effects of Different IASTM Force Applications on Ankle Stiffness and Dorsiflexion
summary:
Instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization (IASTM) is a technique commonly used in sports medicine to reduce muscle tightness and improve range of motion. The technique involves using a handheld instrument, typically made of metal, to apply pressure and massage soft tissues. The instrument allows clinicians to target specific areas while reducing stress on their hands. Previous research has demonstrated that IASTM may improve range of motion and reduce muscle tightness. However, little is known about how the amount of force applied during treatment influences these outcomes. This study aims to investigate the effects of different IASTM treatment forces on calf muscle stiffness and ankle dorsiflexion (the movement of the foot upward toward the shin). Participants will receive either low-force IASTM (0-5 N), high-force IASTM (10-15 N), or no treatment depending on what group they are assigned to. Treatment force will be monitored using a sensor attached to the IASTM instrument (Figure 1). Changes in tissue stiffness will be assessed using the MyotonPRO, a handheld device that measures the mechanical properties of muscles and other soft tissues. Changes in ankle dorsiflexion will be evaluated using clinical movement tests and motion capture analysis.

The findings may help researchers and clinicians better understand how different IASTM treatment protocols influence tissue stiffness and ankle mobility, potentially contributing to more standardized treatment recommendations.
conditions: Range of Motion, Articular, Ankle Joint
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

\- You are between 18 and 39 years of age You are able to stand, walk, squat, and lunge barefoot without assistance You are able to read and understand English and provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

\- You do not have a current skin infection. You do not have any prior lower extremity surgeries for muscles, bones, or joints.

You do not have a current injury that limits your gait or ability to squat. You are not currently pregnant. You are not taking any anticoagulant medications, or medications that would inhibit your balance, or pain perception.

You do not have an allergy to ultrasound gel.
